evidence.positive: Against the running image (0b1fed6c1, container orci-loop-or-3060-orci-1), staged a mayo-mayo patient via the admin API with dob 1951-01-01 (age 75), weight 80 kg, condition c-type-2-diabetes-mellitus (tag DIABETES_TYPE_2), no eGFR observation and no home insulin, plus a GLUCOSE observation of 200 mg/dL inserted 5 minutes before evaluation. POST /api/cds/medication-selection/{pmrn}/{caseId} with m-insulin-regular returned the SUBCUTANEOUS default option '4 units' (Mayo moderate scale, range 180-219) and GET /api/admin/rule/evaluations/fired showed the w-insulin-default-dose firing with details USE_MODERATE_DOSE_SCALE=true, LAST_GLUCOSE=200, SUBCUTANEOUS_RANGE_TEXT='180-219'. Under the old criteria this patient (age 75, no eGFR, no daily insulin) would have been on the low scale.
evidence.negative: Same shape at mayo-mayo without type 2: a patient with no conditions returned '2 units' with USE_MODERATE_DOSE_SCALE=false, and a patient with c-type-1-diabetes-mellitus also returned '2 units' / false. Sites without condition-based criteria are unchanged: the identical patient (type 2, age 75, no eGFR, no insulin) at demo-demo returned '1 units' (default low scale 151-200) with USE_MODERATE_DOSE_SCALE=false; and a demo-demo patient meeting all four default criteria (type 2, dob 1970 so age 56, EGFR observation 60, home insulin note parsed by /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/insulin-daily-dose as '60 units' per day) returned '2 units' (default moderate scale 151-200) with USE_MODERATE_DOSE_SCALE=true. Data flip at Mayo: deleting the type 2 condition from the positive patient and re-selecting gave '2 units' / false; re-adding it gave '4 units' / true. Changeset 248 ran EXECUTED on mayo-mayo and MARK_RAN on demo-demo at boot.

Re-running the Mayo type 2 selection then returned '2 units' with USE_MODERATE_DOSE_SCALE=false (red), and the log carried 'OR-3060 RED CHECK pre-fix criteria active: type2=true under70=false egfrOk=false dailyDoseOk=false' under tenant mayo-mayo; the demo-demo four-criteria patient stayed moderate under the pre-fix class, as expected. caveats: The merged scope is narrower than the ticket text: Mayo's condition-based criteria are 'type 2 diabetes alone' (per the merged spec and PR), so pancreatectomy, dialysis, thin, corticosteroid, tube-feed and parenteral-nutrition inputs and their acceptance-criteria tests are not delivered here; Alex's comment indicates that was expected.

Selection was driven through POST /api/cds/medication-selection (the same controller the dosing form calls) with an admin session; the React dosing form itself was not rendered, and the Mayo case was not started through app-launch (no Epic locally).

Changeset 248 executed at boot against an empty mayo-mayo schema (0 rows); its rescoring logic was exercised by re-running the extracted SQL by hand, where psql warned that SET LOCAL lock_timeout is a no-op outside a transaction (Liquibase runs it inside one).
The pre-fix class used for the red check carries one added WARN log line to mark the path; its moderate-scale decision logic is the parent commit's verbatim.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A Mayo type 2 patient aged 75 with no eGFR and no home insulin got the moderate subcutaneous default of 4 units at glucose 200, with USE_MODERATE_DOSE_SCALE true.
Negative: Mayo patients with no diabetes or type 1 stayed on the low scale at 2 units, and the same type 2 patient shape at a default-criteria site stayed low at 1 unit while a demo patient meeting all four default criteria still got moderate.
Red check: Swapping the pre-fix rule class into the container dropped the Mayo type 2 patient to 2 units with the moderate flag false, and restoring the shipped class brought back 4 units; running changeset 248 by hand rescored the low-scale firing to 4 units and flipped its compliance to false.

Automation: Unit tests already cover the criteria split; proposed a Mayo-tenant end-to-end check, a default-site guard, and a migration test for changeset 248.
